points.quote: The University of Exeter follows a four-tier approach to GenAI use in assessments:
points.gist: Exeter uses a four-tier approach to GenAI use in assessments.

points.quote: You must not use GenAI tools under any circumstances when preparing and writing for this assessment.
points.gist: In AI-prohibited assessments, GenAI tools must not be used under any circumstances.

points.quote: You may use AI tools for checking spelling and grammar mistakes only, with no other impact on the structure or content of the assessment.
points.gist: In AI-minimal assessments, AI tools may be used only for spelling and grammar checks with no other impact on structure or content.

points.quote: Do not copy, paste or paraphrase information from these AI-generated summaries.
points.gist: In AI-minimal assessments, do not copy, paste or paraphrase information from AI-generated summaries in search tools.

points.quote: You must include GenAI prompts and, where possible, hyperlinks to their output as part of your submission.
points.gist: In AI-integrated assessments, submissions must include GenAI prompts and, where possible, hyperlinks to their output.

points.quote: If hyperlinks are not produced through the tools you use, save the AI-generated output in a document that you can easily access later (e.g. on OneDrive).
points.gist: If a tool produces no hyperlinks, save the AI output in an easily accessible document, for example on OneDrive.

points.quote: You must never use AI to translate more than a word or short phrase into English unless agreed in the checked boxes in your assessment brief.
points.gist: AI must never be used to translate more than a word or short phrase into English unless the assessment brief's checked boxes agree.

points.quote: The assessment brief will include a checklist of purposes that AI can be used for.
points.gist: AI-assisted assessment briefs include a checklist of purposes AI can be used for.

points.quote: When you submit your assessment to ELE, you will need to check a box to confirm that you have complied with the University's policy on academic conduct, and with the expectations regarding the use of GenAI as specified in your assessment brief.
points.gist: Submission to ELE requires checking a box confirming compliance with academic conduct policy and the brief's GenAI expectations.

points.quote: You must never upload sensitive or identifying material to an AI tool.
points.anchor: Key points to be aware of
points.gist: Sensitive or identifying material must never be uploaded to an AI tool.

points.quote: You must therefore critically analyse and verify any information that you plan to use in your academic work, including any references or sources provided by a GenAI tool.
points.anchor: Key points to be aware of
points.gist: Students must critically analyse and verify information used in academic work, including references or sources provided by GenAI.

points.quote: The majority of these tools are allowed even in AI-prohibited assignments.
points.gist: Most assistive technology tools using AI are allowed even in AI-prohibited assignments.

points.quote: Please be aware that incorporating Grammarly's suggested edits into your academic work may breach the University's Academic Honesty policy.
points.gist: Incorporating Grammarly's suggested edits into academic work may breach the Academic Honesty policy.

points.quote: Misrepresentation includes misrepresenting an AI generated source as your own work;
points.gist: Misrepresenting an AI-generated source as your own work counts as misrepresentation under the conduct policy.

points.quote: No matter what category of AI use your assessment is, when you finish your work, ask yourself: 'Who is the author of this work?'.
points.gist: Before submitting, ask yourself who the author of the work is.
